title: Alignment in Grid 🎯
description: Align items and tracks using `justify-items`, `align-items`, `justify-content`, `align-content`, and their place shorthands.

slides.title: Two Levels of Alignment 🧭
slides.content:
# Container vs Item Alignment

Grid gives you two sets of alignment properties:
1. **Container‑level** – applies to all items within their grid cells.
   - `justify-items` (inline/row axis, i.e., horizontal)
   - `align-items` (block/column axis, i.e., vertical)
   - `place-items` (shorthand)
2. **Content‑level** – applies to the entire grid tracks when they are smaller than the container.
   - `justify-content` (distributes columns horizontally)
   - `align-content` (distributes rows vertically)
   - `place-content` (shorthand)

And each item can override with `justify-self` and `align-self`.

slides.title: `justify-items` & `align-items` 🎚️
slides.content:
# Align All Items Inside Their Cells

Default is `stretch` (items fill the cell). Values: `start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch`.

```css
.container {
  justify-items: center; /* all items horizontally centred in their columns */
  align-items: end;     /* all items placed at the bottom of their rows */
}
```
`place-items` is shorthand: `place-items: center;` (both axes) or `place-items: center start;` (align-items, justify-items).

quizData.question: What does `place-items: center stretch;` do?

options.text: Centres items vertically and stretches them horizontally
Centres items horizontally and stretches them vertically
Centres items on the row axis and stretches them on the column axis (align-items: center; justify-items: stretch;)

quizData.explanation: The first value is for `align-items` (column axis), second for `justify-items` (row axis). So center aligns vertically, stretch stretches horizontally.

slides.title: `justify-self` & `align-self` (Item Level) 🤸
slides.content:
# Override Alignment for a Single Item

Just like Flexbox, grid items can override the container's `justify-items`/`align-items` with their own `justify-self`/`align-self`.

```css
.item {
  justify-self: end;   /* pinned to right of its column */
  align-self: center; /* centred vertically within its row */
}
```
Useful for positioning one element differently from its siblings.

quizData.question: `justify-content: space-between;` only works if the grid tracks have a total size smaller than the container.
quizData.explanation: `justify-content` distributes leftover space; if tracks fill the container, there's no leftover space to distribute.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `place-` Shorthands

`place-items` and `place-content` let you set both axes in one line. They're supported everywhere Grid is.
